children: For the second day in a row, strong auction of longer-term Treasurys has provided a bit of an afternoon relief to the bond market. Yields on longer-term Treasurys remain much higher on the day. But they have come a bit further off their session highs after a $22 billion auction of 30-year bonds met with solid demand from investors. Reflecting that demand, the bonds were sold at a lower yield than traders had anticipated, and banks that are required to bid took down a record low share of the auction, according to BMO.

Yields on 30-year Treasurys fell the most after the auction, recently hovering around 5.330%, according to Tradeweb. However, the 10-year yield was roughly unchanged at 4.924%. And yields on short-term Treasurys, which have led the move higher Thursday, actually ticked higher after the auction.
